name: Thalavar
description: Thalavar is a precision neuromodulator that interfaces directly with BCI reward-pathway firmware to trigger sustained, tiered dopamine and endorphin cascades without depleting natural reserves. Unlike crude stimulants, it maps the user's existing pleasure-response architecture and amplifies it — meaning every user's high is uniquely their own. Marketed in Tier 3-4 as a 'wellness supplement,' it is quietly one of Lazarus's highest-revenue products.
effects: profound euphoria tailored to individual neurotype
BCI-users report visual 'warmth overlay' on their HUD
side_effects: BCI firmware drift if used more than twice weekly
rare: reward-circuit lock (user finds nothing pleasurable without the drug)
cultural_context: Thalavar is the corporate world's open secret — Tier 3 and 4 professionals use it to survive the grind, to feel something after sixty-hour weeks. It's taken at home, quietly, with a glass of something warm. Nobody talks about it at the office but everyone knows. On the Shelf, bootleg Thal cut with industrial solvents circulates as 'Deepfire' and causes significantly higher rates of reward-circuit lock.
story_hooks: A Tier 3 mid-manager realizes they haven't felt anything without Thalavar in eight months — and their prescription just got flagged for review after a workplace incident
Lazarus's internal data shows reward-circuit lock rates are three times higher than their published figures; someone on the research team wants to leak it
A Shelf chemist has reverse-engineered Thalavar but the bootleg version has a 1-in-40 chance of permanent anhedonia — and she's selling it anyway because people are desperate
